input: Pack a hospital bag at thirty-six weeks pregnant

gold.taskTitle: Pack a hospital bag at thirty-six weeks
gold.taskDescription: Prepare a fully packed hospital bag before the baby arrives, covering all items needed for labour, delivery, and postpartum stay.

questions.title: Is this your first baby or a subsequent one?
questions.description: First-time parents often need more guidance on what to pack, while experienced parents may already have a checklist.

questions.title: Are you planning a vaginal birth or a C-section?
questions.description: The type of delivery significantly changes what clothing, comfort items, and recovery supplies are needed.

questions.title: How many nights do you expect to stay in hospital?
questions.description: An expected short stay versus a longer one changes the quantity of clothing, toiletries, and snacks to pack.

questions.title: Are you planning to breastfeed or bottle-feed?
questions.description: Feeding choice determines whether nursing bras, breast pads, nipple cream, or formula supplies need to be included.

questions.title: Does your hospital provide any items like nappies or towels?
questions.description: Knowing what the hospital supplies prevents overpacking and helps identify gaps.

questions.title: Do you have a birth partner staying with you throughout?
questions.description: A birth partner's needs, such as snacks, a phone charger, or a change of clothes, may need to be packed too.

questions.title: Do you have any medical conditions requiring specific items?
questions.description: Conditions such as gestational diabetes, a planned induction, or a NICU possibility may require additional specialist items.
